action.details: Assemble the four native strokes over source-observed sail, mast and hull cages with one distant-vessel plate and a source-keyed dinghy.

critic.gap: The main sail has been redrawn into a broad triangle crossed by a central mast. In design.png the sail sits to the left of, and terminates at, the irregular doubled right-edge mast. That distinctive sail/mast relationship is lost in every key, so the result reads as a generic sailboat doodle rather than the original QuickDraw drawing animated.
protected_strengths: The source's clear growth from a fully visible boat to a large top/right-cropped close approach across all nine pairs.
The matched lateral movement and late framing, including the trailing small boat and sparse distant boats as spatial cues.
The simple doodle treatment and recognizable angular hull outline without added visual complexity.

action.details: Restore the original mast-to-sail trailing-edge relationship without changing the observed approach, scale, lateral travel or crop.

critic.gap: The original doodle has a distinct near-upright mast extending from the sail peak into the middle of the hull. In every current key, that structural stroke instead follows the long sloping right sail edge and protrudes diagonally beyond it, so the boat loses the most recognizable mast-and-sail relationship of the original QuickDraw drawing.
protected_strengths: The nine pairs preserve the source approach, increasing scale, late top/right cropping, and boat position well enough for the source framing/pose bar.
Preserve the sparse unfilled polygonal doodle treatment and simple hull; do not add realistic sail or hull detail.
Preserve the small trailing dinghy and background boats as secondary cues without increasing their visual weight.

action.details: Restore original near-upright mast and single sail to its left, matching the source central mast/left sail; do not invent the source right-hand jib as an extra doodle part.

critic.gap: Source pose: the prominent source sail spreads to both sides of the mast, whereas the rendered sail ends at the mast. In pairs 01 through 06 this omits a large right-hand part of the source silhouette and makes the boat read as a narrow single-sided sail rather than the source barge. The approach, hull placement, growth, and late frame exit otherwise track the source convincingly. The original QuickDraw identity remains legible in the triangular sail, doubled irregular mast, angular open-top hull, and unpolished thin contour.
protected_strengths: The recognizable original triangular sail, slightly doubled crooked mast, and irregular angular hull.
Thin uneven doodle outlines and sparse visual detail.
The source-matched approach, increasing scale, late top/right cropping, and small trailing dinghy.
The clear separation between the main dark boat and faint background boats and water marks.
